Order: Hymenoptera

I found this particular wasp on my driveway resting in the shaded area. Upon further examination I noticed that there were many others as well. The wasps seemed to prefer the shaded areas of the concrete driveway as opposed to the sunlit ones. I observed that the wasps were resting individually, as well as, in clusters of around 2-4 wasps interacting with one another, which speaks to their social nature. 

Physical features of this particular wasp:
Size: ~ 2.5 cm
Eyes: 2 large compound eyes
Legs: 6 relatively thin segmented legs
Antennae: long, with gradient colouration (yellow to dark brown/black). 
Colouration: typical “Yellowjacket” colouring with black and yellow stripes with the distinguishing factor which was the reddish colouring found near the head region. This wasp had more yellow pigmentation as compared to the others observed in the same area. I also saw that some of the other wasps had no reddish colouring. 

Behaviour:
The wasp was relatively aggressive when approached and responded quickly to external stimuli often by flying away. 

Host Plants:
Although, I did not see this particular wasp on or near a plant. I did notice that many of the other wasps were found near the flowering plants (rose bushes) in the garden which was right off of the driveway.

description: Showed some odd behavior. It was in the doorway of my art studio, so I needed to move it to a safer spot. Upon introductions, it tried to bite my fingernail, but soon calmed down and allowed me to pet it. it started off a bit sluggish, but became active and started spinning- just turning around in circles in place. It drifted towards the edge of a stair step and fell off, and I helped it right itself. It resumed spinning. I interacted with it, trying to see if it needed help, and it stepped over my fingernail multiple times to continue spinning in place. It fell off another step, and had a harder time getting upright; it seemed very clumsy and almost drunk. I helped it up again and more, slower spinning. It was strange because it seemed coordinated about stepping past my finger but otherwise cery disoriented. Not knowing what it was doing or if it needed help, I carefully picked it up and set it down in a safe area that has plenty of good potential hibernation spots
